items.title: USCIS changed Form I-765 paper filing locations (incl. F-1 OPT)
items.summary: Effective 2026-10-07, USCIS changed lockbox filing addresses for mailed Form I-765. Standalone paper I-765 for F-1 OPT categories (c)(3)(A) pre-completion, (c)(3)(B) post-completion, and (c)(3)(C) STEM OPT goes to USCIS Chicago Lockbox (USPS Attn I-765 C03, P.O. Box 805373, Chicago, IL 60680-5374; courier Attn I-765 C03 (Box 805373), 131 S. Dearborn, 3rd Floor, Chicago, IL 60603-5517). 30-day grace: forms postmarked on or before 2026-11-09 to any prior location still accepted. Wrong post-grace address may delay or risk rejection. Online filing and fee amounts unchanged by this alert. Same-day changes also hit I-539 and other forms. In effect for new mailings.
affected: current F-1 filing paper OPT/STEM OPT I-765
items.slate_impact: Low for Fall 2027 applicants now (OPT years away); material process risk for anyone mailing OPT I-765 before/after the 2026-11-09 grace end.

items.title: DHS finalizes removal of automatic EAD extensions (certain categories)
items.summary: Final rule 2026-20955 (91 FR 65306), effective 2026-10-14, reaffirms the Oct 30, 2025 IFR: for covered categories, a timely I-765 renewal filed on/after 2025-10-30 does not automatically extend an expired/expiring EAD (limited statutory/TPS exceptions). USCIS OPT page still states that a timely STEM OPT I-765 yields a separate 180-day employment-authorization bridge while pending. Northeastern OGS note (IFR-day) says the change does not impact F-1 STEM OPT extension 180-day bridge. Not legal advice; student-category edge cases developing.
affected: EAD renewal filers in covered 274a.12(c) categories
F-1 OPT/STEM applicants (STEM bridge appears intact per USCIS OPT page)
items.slate_impact: Fall 2027 post-grad OPT/STEM path: do not assume general auto-EAD extension; STEM 180-day bridge still described by USCIS.

items.title: USCIS proposes removing deference to prior eligibility determinations on extensions
items.summary: NPRM 2026-20941 published 2026-10-14 would remove 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5) deference when adjudicating requests to extend a petition for employment/stay (same facts). Comments due 2026-11-13. Not in effect. Primary path is employment-based I-129 extensions (e.g. H-1B), i.e. post-OPT pipeline, not F-1 study admission.
affected: F-1 alumni later on H-1B/other worker categories
items.slate_impact: Adjacent watch for Fall 2027 → OPT → H-1B path; could raise extension RFEs/denials if finalized. Not a current F-1 study-rule change.
